newsitem.title: CANADA: INSTANT VIEW - Canada April unemployment.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Canada April unemployment.

text.p: Following are reactions to April unemployment data released by Statistics Canada on Friday. Statistics Canada, in its last such release before the June 2 federal election, said on Friday the unemployment rate rose to 9.6 percent in April from 9.3 percent in March.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to remain unchanged.
Michael Gregory, economist, Lehman Brothers - "Kind of a mixed bag here. The employment number was good, a good solid number. A 33,000 gain -- more than what people were expecting.
"I think it shows, on the back of the 61,000 from the previous month, that there is some reasonable job creation going on in Canada. That's the good news.

"It seems to be encouraging a lot of people who were out of the labor force to come back in the labor force. The labor force participation rate rose and the labor force was up sharply and, as a result, the unemployment rate -- which during a federal election, matters a heck of a lot because it's one number you can wrap your mind around -- rose three ticks from 9.3 to 9.6 (percent).

"On balance, this is a good report. It shows that the Canadian economy may be finally moving in a self-propogating mode where internal job growth fuels consumption which then keeps the process going."

Randall Powley, senior economist, ScotiaMcLeod Inc -- "We were looking for some sort of increase in the unemployment rate...Given the strong growth in the help-wanted index and the improving conditions overall in the economy, there should (have been) a lot more people coming back into the labor force (than there have been the past year).

"I would say (the report) was neutral to positive. Employment has been way behind the rest of the economy...The month before, it was growing at 1.1 percent year-on-year. Given the rest of the numbers, it should be growing at least 3.0 percent and actually closer to 4.0. So I would expect to see a string of fairly solid employment numbers in through the next three or four months at least."

Paul Ferley, assistant chief economist, Bank of Montreal -- "The growth in employment was maybe a little bit weaker than what we were expecting. But it still showed a solid increase and suggests that the economy created almost 100,000 jobs in two months, which is a pretty good record.

"As well, we weren't expecting quite as large a jump in the unemployment rate although that reflected more people being encouraged to come back into the labor force, which one can still view as an encouraging sign.

"So on net, I think the report is still consistent with improving economic conditions, maybe not quite as rapidly as we had expected. But still I think the trend in the economy is upwards and improvement in the labor markets are upwards."
